prompt: What is a carbonyl group?

choices.text: An O atom joined to a C atom by a double bond
An OH group bonded to a carbon
choices.why: That is the alcohol functional group. A carbonyl is C=O.

choices.text: An O atom bonded to two carbon groups by single bonds
choices.why: That is an ether, R–O–R′.

choices.text: A carbon atom with three H atoms
choices.why: That's a methyl group. The carbonyl group is C=O.

explanation: The carbonyl group is formed when an O atom and a C atom are joined by a double bond. What the other two bonds of the C atom are attached to determines the type of compound.

prompt: What makes a molecule an aldehyde?

choices.text: One bond of the carbonyl carbon is to an H atom, so the carbonyl group is at the end of a carbon chain.
The carbonyl group is in the middle of a carbon chain.
choices.why: That is a ketone.

choices.text: It has a carbonyl group bonded to an OH group.
choices.why: That's the carboxyl group of a carboxylic acid.

choices.text: It has an O atom bonded to two carbon groups.
choices.why: That's an ether.

explanation: If one bond of the carbonyl group is made to an H atom, the molecule is an aldehyde. The main thing to note is that the carbonyl group is at the end of a carbon chain.

prompt: What makes a molecule a ketone?

choices.text: Its carbonyl group is in the middle of a carbon chain, with both remaining bonds to C atoms.
Its carbonyl group is at the end of a chain, bonded to an H atom.
choices.why: That is an aldehyde.

choices.text: It has an OH group bonded to a carbon.
choices.why: That is an alcohol.

choices.text: It is any molecule with an oxygen atom.
choices.why: Many functional groups contain oxygen. A ketone has a C=O in the middle of a chain.

explanation: A carbonyl group in the middle of a carbon chain, with both remaining bonds to C atoms, makes the molecule a ketone. Aldehydes and ketones share the carbonyl group but have different properties.

prompt: What suffix is used in naming aldehydes?

choices.why: -ol is the suffix for alcohols. Don't confuse -al with -ol.
-one is the suffix for ketones.
-oic acid is the suffix for carboxylic acids.

explanation: Aldehydes are named with the parent hydrocarbon name plus the suffix -al, with the carbonyl carbon numbered 1. Do not confuse -al with -ol, the alcohol suffix.

prompt: A student writes "propanal" for CH3CH2CH2OH. What is wrong?

choices.text: CH3CH2CH2OH is an alcohol, so its name ends in -ol: 1-propanol. Propanal is an aldehyde.

choices.why: -one is for ketones. This molecule has an OH group: it is an alcohol.

choices.text: Nothing is wrong; -al and -ol mean the same thing.
choices.why: -al marks an aldehyde (C=O at the end of a chain); -ol marks an alcohol (OH).

choices.text: The name should be propanoic acid.
choices.why: That would need a carboxyl group. This molecule has an OH group on a carbon.

explanation: The suffix -al marks an aldehyde and -ol an alcohol. CH3CH2CH2OH has an OH group on carbon 1: 1-propanol.

prompt: What suffix is used in naming ketones?

choices.why: -al is for aldehydes.
-ene is for alkenes.
-ol is for alcohols.

explanation: When naming a ketone, take the name of the parent hydrocarbon and change the suffix to -one; larger ketones need a number for the carbonyl position.

prompt: A four-carbon chain has an aldehyde group (C=O bonded to H) at one end. What is its name?

choices.why: -ol is for alcohols. An aldehyde ends in -al.
-one is for ketones, with the carbonyl in the middle.
The carbonyl carbon counts in the chain, so there are four carbons: butanal.

explanation: The main chain includes the carbonyl carbon, which is numbered 1. Four carbons with an aldehyde group gives butanal.

prompt: A six-carbon chain has a carbonyl group on its second carbon. What is its name?

choices.why: An aldehyde's carbonyl is at the end (carbon 1). One on carbon 2 makes a ketone: -one.
Number from the end nearer the carbonyl: 2.
-ol is for an OH group. A carbonyl in the middle of the chain makes a ketone.

explanation: A carbonyl in the middle of a chain makes a ketone (-one), and a number shows its position, as low as possible: 2-hexanone.

prompt: A seven-carbon chain has a carbonyl group on the fifth carbon counting from the left. What is its name?

choices.why: Number from the right to give the carbonyl the lower number: 3.
With the carbonyl in the middle of the chain, it's a ketone: -one.
The chain has seven carbons: heptanone.

explanation: Counting from the right, the carbonyl is on carbon 3, so the ketone is 3-heptanone.

prompt: Methanal has a familiar common name. What is it?

choices.why: Acetone is propanone, a ketone.
Formic acid is methanoic acid, a carboxylic acid.
Methanol is an alcohol. Methanal is the aldehyde formaldehyde.

explanation: Methanal, the one-carbon aldehyde, has the common name formaldehyde.

prompt: What is the common name for propanone, the smallest ketone?

choices.why: Formaldehyde is methanal, an aldehyde.
Acetic acid is ethanoic acid, a carboxylic acid.
Ethyl alcohol is ethanol.

explanation: The common name for propanone is acetone; it can also be called dimethyl ketone.

prompt: How many carbon atoms does the smallest possible ketone have?
explanation: A ketone's carbonyl must be bonded to a carbon on each side, so the smallest ketone has three carbons: propanone.

prompt: Ketones can also be named by their alkyl groups plus the word ketone. What is 3-pentanone called this way?

choices.why: Dimethyl ketone is propanone. 3-pentanone has an ethyl group on each side of the carbonyl.
That is 2-pentanone, with the carbonyl on carbon 2.
Name the two groups on either side of the carbonyl: two ethyl groups.

explanation: In 3-pentanone, the carbonyl carbon is in the middle, with a two-carbon ethyl group on each side: diethyl ketone.

prompt: What is the carboxyl group?

choices.text: The combination of a carbonyl group and an OH group
A carbonyl group bonded to an H atom
choices.why: That makes an aldehyde.

choices.text: Two OH groups on one carbon
choices.why: The carboxyl group combines C=O with OH on the same carbon.

choices.text: An O atom between two carbon groups
choices.why: That is an ether.

explanation: The combination of a carbonyl group and an OH group makes the carboxyl group. Molecules with it are carboxylic acids, and like aldehydes, the group is at the end of a carbon chain.

prompt: A four-carbon chain ends in a carboxyl group. What is its name?

choices.why: The carboxyl carbon counts as one of the chain's carbons: four carbons is butanoic acid.
Butanol is an alcohol. A carboxylic acid ends in -oic acid.
Carboxylic acids are named with the parent name plus -oic acid.

explanation: The C atom of the carboxyl group counts in the parent name, and the suffix -oic acid is added: butanoic acid.

prompt: Which carboxylic acid makes certain ant bites sting?

choices.why: Acetic acid is the active substance in vinegar.
The section names formic acid as the acid in ant bites.
HCl isn't a carboxylic acid. Formic acid causes the sting of some ant bites.

explanation: Methanoic acid and ethanoic acid are also called formic acid and acetic acid. Formic acid makes certain ant bites sting, while acetic acid is the active substance in vinegar.

prompt: How strong are carboxylic acids?

choices.text: All carboxylic acids are weak acids; none is on the list of strong acids.

choices.why: No carboxylic acid approaches the 100% dissociation that defines a strong acid.
They do act as acids, losing the H of the carboxyl group to bases; they're just weak.

choices.text: Only the largest ones are strong.
choices.why: No carboxylic acid is strong; even trichloroacetic acid is only about 45% dissociated.

explanation: No carboxylic acid is on the list of strong acids, so all carboxylic acids are weak acids. A 1 M solution of acetic acid is only about 0.4% ionized.

prompt: A 1.0 M solution of acetic acid is about 0.4% dissociated. What is [H^+] in the solution?
explanation: 0.4% is 0.004 in decimal form: [H^+] = 0.004 × 1.0 M = 0.004 M, far less than the 1.0 M a strong acid would give.

prompt: A 1.0 M solution of formic acid is about 1.3% dissociated. What is [H^+] in the solution?
explanation: [H^+] = 0.013 × 1.0 M = 0.013 M. Formic acid ionizes a little more than acetic acid, but it's still a weak acid.

prompt: What happens when a carboxylic acid reacts with a base such as OH^−?

choices.text: The H atom of the carboxyl group comes off as H^+, leaving a carboxylate anion, and water forms.
The OH of the carboxyl group leaves, forming a cation.
choices.why: The acid loses its H^+, not its OH, leaving a negative carboxylate ion.
Esters form from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol. With a base, the acid forms a carboxylate ion.

choices.text: No reaction occurs, because carboxylic acids are weak.
choices.why: Weak acids still react with bases; the H of the carboxyl group is removed.

explanation: In the presence of bases, carboxylic acids act like acids: the H atom in the carboxyl group comes off as H^+, leaving a carboxylate anion. With OH^−, water also forms.

prompt: Butanoic acid loses its carboxyl H^+ to a base. What is the anion called?

choices.why: Carboxylate ions are named by replacing -oic acid with -oate.
Butanol is an alcohol. The anion of butanoic acid is butanoate.
Replace -oic acid with -oate: butanoate.

explanation: Carboxylate ions are named from the acid name: -oic acid is replaced with -oate. Butanoic acid gives the butanoate ion.

prompt: How is an ester formed?

choices.text: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol combine, removing a water molecule.
A carboxylic acid reacts with a base.
choices.why: That gives a carboxylate salt and water, not an ester.

choices.text: An alcohol loses water to form a double bond.
choices.why: That's elimination, which gives an alkene.
An ester needs an acid and an alcohol: the acid supplies one side, the alcohol the other.

explanation: When a carboxylic acid and an alcohol are combined under the proper conditions, a water molecule is removed and the remaining pieces combine to form the ester functional group.

prompt: What ester forms from ethanol and butanoic acid?

choices.why: The alkyl name comes from the alcohol (ethanol → ethyl) and the -oate name from the acid (butanoic → butanoate).
Esters are named with the alcohol's alkyl group plus the acid's carboxylate name.
An ether has an O between two alkyl groups; this product is an ester.

explanation: Esters are named with the alkyl group from the alcohol plus the carboxylate name from the acid: ethanol + butanoic acid gives ethyl butanoate, which smells of banana.

prompt: A student names the ester made from methanol and ethanoic acid as "ethyl methanoate". What is wrong?

choices.text: The alkyl name comes from the alcohol and the -oate from the acid: methyl ethanoate.

choices.why: The acid part is named as a carboxylate: ethanoate.
That's a ketone. An acid and an alcohol make an ester.
The student swapped the parts: methanol gives methyl, and ethanoic acid gives ethanoate.

explanation: The acid contributes one side and the alcohol the other. Esters are named alcohol's alkyl group + acid's carboxylate name: methyl ethanoate.

prompt: Why are esters used in foods and perfumes?

choices.text: Many esters have very pleasant odors and flavors.
Esters are strong acids that preserve food.
choices.why: Esters aren't acids. Many are valued for pleasant smells and tastes.

choices.text: Esters are good sources of protein.
choices.why: Esters are used for odors and flavors; many artificial flavorings are esters.
Their value is in their odors and flavors, contributing to the smell of flowers and taste of fruits.

explanation: Many esters have very pleasant odors and flavors and contribute to the odor of flowers and the taste of fruits; artificial flavorings are often esters.

prompt: What is the ether functional group?

choices.text: An O atom bonded to two organic groups, R–O–R′

choices.why: That's a carbonyl group.

choices.text: An OH group bonded to a carbon
choices.why: That's an alcohol.

choices.text: A carbonyl bonded to an O–R group
choices.why: That's an ester.

explanation: The ether functional group is an O atom bonded to two organic groups, R–O–R′. The two R groups may be the same or different.

prompt: What is the name of CH3CH2OCH2CH3?

choices.why: Dimethyl ether is CH3OCH3. Here each side of the O is a two-carbon ethyl group.
Butanol has an OH group; this molecule has an O between two carbon groups.
An ester has a carbonyl next to the O. This is an ether.

explanation: Ethers are named by naming the R groups and appending the word ether. Two ethyl groups on the O make diethyl ether, once used as an anesthetic.

prompt: What is the name of CH3OCH2CH2CH3?

choices.why: Only one side is propyl; the other is a one-carbon methyl group.
That would be an ester, with a carbonyl next to the O. This is an ether.
1-butanol has an OH group. This molecule has an O bonded to two carbon groups.

explanation: Name the two groups on the O and add the word ether: a methyl group and a propyl group give methyl propyl ether.
